answer: Epoch close freezes each node's state root: it commits a unique Blake3 hash over its dedicated 16 GB RAM array, seeded per-epoch so roots cannot be copied forward. Verifiers reread a random sample of those arrays live and match the fresh hash; a replay from a shared pool yields mismatched pigment across two runs. First failure quarantines the identity, second burns its stake. Forging 5000 identities needs 80 TB of distinct RAM at roughly $240000 monthly, a tundra of cost no fable of cheap fakery survives.
